title_en: Kunming Oke Commerce & Trade Co., Ltd. and Xiong Zhimin v. Li Changyou et al. — dispute over confirmation of shareholder qualification
ruling_gist_en: Where a transaction is titled as equity transfer, but the fund flows between the parties exhibit characteristics of a loan relationship, with conditions such as the return of equity upon debt repayment, the transferee not taking over company management after the transfer, and the expression of an intention to provide security, and where the transferee does not enjoy shareholder rights, it shall be identified as an equity transfer for security. The transferee in an equity transfer for security is only a nominal shareholder and does not actually enjoy shareholder rights. If the transferor (the security provider) requests confirmation of its ownership of the equity, such request shall be supported. However, before the secured debt is fully repaid, a request by the transferor to change the equity registration to its own name shall not be supported.

full_text_en:
Kunming Ouke Commercial Trading Co., Ltd. and Xiong Zhimin v. Li Changyou et al. — Dispute over Confirmation of Shareholder Qualification

【Ruling Summary】

Where a transaction is in the form of an equity transfer, but the flow of funds between the transferor and transferee is characterized by a loan relationship, the existence of conditions such as the return of the equity upon repayment of the debt, the transferee's failure to take over management of the company after the transfer, and expressions indicating an intention to provide security, all of which are inconsistent with the transferee enjoying shareholder rights, the transaction shall be deemed an equity transfer for security purposes. The holder of the equity for security purposes is only a nominal shareholder and does not actually enjoy shareholder rights. A request by the transferor for security to confirm its ownership of the equity shall be upheld. However, before the secured debt is fully repaid, a request by the transferor for security to register the equity in its own name shall not be upheld.

When adjudicating disputes involving equity transfers for security, the people's court should carefully examine the specific provisions of the relevant contracts, accurately ascertain the true intent of the parties, and fully respect the parties' autonomy of will. It should also accurately determine whether an equity transfer for security exists by referring to the legal requirements for pledge of rights. Whether the operation of the company has been transferred is not an essential element. In cases involving the transfer of company operation, the court should take into comprehensive consideration factors such as the security holder's investment and operational contributions, market conditions, and apply the principle of balancing interests to properly resolve disputes arising from operational profits or losses, changes in equity value, and other related issues.

Plaintiff: Xiong Zhimin, male, Han Chinese, born on May 18, 1964, residing in Xishan District, Kunming City, Yunnan Province.

Plaintiff: Kunming Ouke Commercial Trading Co., Ltd., domiciled at Kunming Yuanbo Impression Tourism Cultural City, Panlong District, Kunming City, Yunnan Province.
Legal Representative: Fu Kun, General Manager of the company.

Defendant: Yu Xiaoping, male, Han Chinese, born on April 28, 1956, residing in Zhushan District, Jingdezhen City, Jiangxi Province.

Defendant: Xu Ying, female, Han Chinese, born on May 9, 1983, residing in Changjiang District, Jingdezhen City, Jiangxi Province.

Third Party: Li Changyou, male, Han Chinese, born on December 25, 1962, residing on Changnan Avenue, Jingdezhen City.

Plaintiff Xiong Zhimin and Plaintiff Kunming Ouke Commercial Trading Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Ouke Company") filed a lawsuit with the Intermediate People's Court of Jingdezhen City, Jiangxi Province, against Defendants Yu Xiaoping and Xu Ying, and Third Party Li Changyou, regarding a dispute over confirmation of shareholder qualification.

The Plaintiffs, Xiong Zhimin and Ouke Company, alleged: In November 2014, the Plaintiffs borrowed RMB 8 million from the Defendants Yu Xiaoping and Xu Ying for use in the Hongrong Company project. When the loan matured, they were unable to repay on time. Yu Xiaoping and Xu Ying then proposed that they could continue lending, but required the equity of Jingdezhen Hongrong Real Estate Development Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as "Hongrong Company") to be transferred to Yu Xiaoping and Xu Ying as security for the loan. On December 2, 2014, Xiong Zhimin and Ouke Company respectively entered into "Equity Transfer Agreements" with Yu Xiaoping and Xu Ying, and completed the registration of the equity transfer. Thereafter, Xiong Zhimin and Ouke Company continued to exercise the rights of company shareholders, while Yu Xiaoping and Xu Ying never paid any equity transfer consideration. Subsequently, Yu Xiaoping and Xu Ying provided additional loans totaling RMB 65,294,000 to Xiong Zhimin. Xiong Zhimin issued 33 promissory notes for the above loans and issued a letter of commitment for interest, and all the above loans were used in the Hongrong Company project. The actual controller behind Yu Xiaoping and Xu Ying is the Third Party, Li Changyou. The Plaintiffs claimed that Hongrong Company had been forcibly occupied and requested confirmation of their equity and an order for the industrial and commercial registration to be changed to their names.

The Defendants, Yu Xiaoping and Xu Ying, argued in defense: Although the RMB 73,294,000 in question was covered by promissory notes, in substance, RMB 10 million was the equity transfer consideration, RMB 22,872,000 was compensation for the initial investment of the Plaintiffs, RMB 1.6 million was remuneration for Xiong Zhimin, and RMB 38,822,000 was project investment. The "Equity Transfer Agreements" reflected the true intent of the parties. Xu Ying and Yu Xiaoping paid the transfer consideration, completed the industrial and commercial registration changes, and lawfully acquired the equity.

The Third Party, Li Changyou, argued: He agreed with the opinions of Defendants Yu Xiaoping and Xu Ying.

The following facts were found by the court of first instance, the Intermediate People's Court of Jingdezhen City, Jiangxi Province:

Hongrong Company was established with investment from the Plaintiff Ouke Company and Xiong Zhimin, with a registered capital of RMB 10 million. Ouke Company subscribed for a capital contribution of RMB 5.1 million, representing a 51% shareholding. Xiong Zhimin subscribed for a capital contribution of RMB 4.9 million, representing a 49% shareholding. On December 2, 2014, Xiong Zhimin and the Defendant Yu Xiaoping entered into an "Equity Transfer Agreement," which stipulated that Xiong Zhimin would transfer his 49% equity in Hongrong Company to Yu Xiaoping for a transfer price of RMB 4.9 million. On the same day, Ouke Company and the Defendant Xu Ying entered into an "Equity Transfer Agreement," which stipulated that Ouke Company would transfer its 51% equity in Hongrong Company to Xu Ying for a transfer price of RMB 5.1 million. On December 23, 2014, the shareholder registration change for Hongrong Company was completed, and the legal representative was changed to Xu Ying. At the same time, Hongrong Company's company seal was handed over to Xu Ying and Yu Xiaoping. Between November 3, 2011, and August 14, 2015, Li Changyou, Xu Ying, Yu Xiaoping, Feng Xiaoping, Li Aizhen, Min Dongxiang, Zhang Wan, and others remitted funds totaling RMB 73,294,000 to Changjiang Comprehensive Agricultural Wholesale Market, Liu Hongmei, Yao Biaohua, Hongrong Company, Fuzhou Linchuan Housing Construction Engineering Company, and others.

The Intermediate People's Court of Jingdezhen City, Jiangxi Province, held in the first instance:

The "Equity Transfer Agreements" entered into between Plaintiffs Xiong Zhimin and Ouke Company and Defendants Xu Ying and Yu Xiaoping were the true intent of the parties, did not violate the mandatory provisions of laws and administrative regulations, and were valid contracts. The parties completed the registration of the equity change, and the equity transfer took legal effect. An equity transfer for security is a form of security where, to secure the performance of a debt, the debtor or a third party transfers its equity to the creditor and completes the registration of change. If the debtor fails to perform the debt when due, the creditor may have a priority right to be satisfied from the equity. A security arrangement must have clear and specific provisions regarding the security subject and content; otherwise, it does not constitute an expression of intent for security. During the proceedings, Li Changyou, Xu Ying, and Yu Xiaoping denied the existence of a loan relationship between the parties. Xiong Zhimin and Ouke Company failed to provide effective evidence proving that the parties intended to create an equity transfer for security. The audio recordings provided by Xiong Zhimin only evidenced negotiations between the parties but did not clearly define the rights and obligations of the parties and could not be relied upon as a basis for the judgment. The parties entered into the "Equity Transfer Agreements" and completed the equity registration change. Xu Ying and Yu Xiaoping also paid the contractual consideration. Since Xiong Zhimin and Ouke Company requested the court to find the relationship to be one of transfer for security and demanded the return of the equity, but provided insufficient evidence, the court did not support their claims. Xu Ying, Yu Xiaoping, and Li Changyou claimed that they had paid RMB 73,294,000, of which RMB 10 million was the equity transfer consideration paid by Xu Ying and Yu Xiaoping, RMB 22,872,000 was compensation for Xiong Zhimin's prior investment, RMB 1.6 million was remuneration for re-employing Xiong Zhimin, and the remaining funds were investment payments by Li Changyou, Xu Ying, and Yu Xiaoping for the "Chuangxiang Tiandi" project. Both parties confirmed that the above RMB 73,294,000 had been invested in the "Chuangxiang Tiandi" project. Xiong Zhimin and Ouke Company claimed that they had invested nearly RMB 100 million in the "Chuangxiang Tiandi" project and that the RMB 73,294,000 was a loan they obtained from Li Changyou and others. Xu Ying, Yu Xiaoping, and Li Changyou claimed that in addition to the RMB 73,294,000 already paid, substantial funds had been invested in the subsequent phases of the project, which could be verified by evidence. All parties claimed to have made capital contributions to the "Chuangxiang Tiandi" project. Whether these contributions created other legal relationships was outside the scope of this case, and the parties could assert their rights separately. The claims of Xiong Zhimin and Ouke Company could not be sustained.

Accordingly, the Intermediate People's Court of Jingdezhen City, Jiangxi Province, pursuant to Articles 8, 44, and 60 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China and Articles 134 and 142 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, rendered a judgment on December 24, 2019:

Dismissing all claims of Plaintiffs Xiong Zhimin and Ouke Company.

Xiong Zhimin and Ouke Company, dissatisfied with the judgment of first instance, appealed to the High People's Court of Jiangxi Province, arguing: 1. The RMB 73,294,000 between the appellants and the appellees constituted a private loan. The parties did not have a genuine equity transfer, and the court of first instance erred in not finding the existence of a private loan relationship. 2. The legal relationship between the appellants and the appellees was one of transfer for security. The court of first instance, by only considering partial facts and solely on the ground that "a security arrangement must have clear and specific provisions regarding the security subject and content," denied the existence of a transfer-for-security legal relationship between the appellants and the appellees and erroneously concluded that there was an equity transfer. This constituted unclear fact-finding and incorrect application of law by adjudicating the case as an equity transfer dispute. 3. The dismissal of the appellants' claims by the court of first instance violated the fundamental principle of fairness and justice, infringed upon the appellants' lawful rights and interests, and protected the appellees' illegal interests. The appellants had purchased all equity of Hongrong Company from its former shareholders for RMB 51.08 million and, after acquiring Hongrong Company, had invested over RMB 100 million. The company was operating normally and had project assets worth over RMB 300 million. The appellees, by providing loans, induced the appellants to transfer the equity to them, with the intention of acquiring the appellants' equity in Hongrong Company, which had assets worth over RMB 300 million, for only RMB 10 million. This conduct was in essence an illegal "collateralized loan trap." The judgment of first instance, by dismissing the appellants' claims, allowed the appellees to acquire all equity of Hongrong Company, worth over RMB 300 million, for only RMB 10 million, contravening the basic principle of fairness and justice that judicial activities should follow and harming the appellants' lawful rights and interests.

Yu Xiaoping and Xu Ying argued in defense: 1. The appellants did not provide objective evidence supporting their claim that there was an agreement between the parties to transfer the equity of Hongrong Company to the appellees as security for a loan. 2. The existence of promissory notes does not necessarily mean that the legal relationship between the parties was one of private lending. During the evidentiary hearing of the court hearing, the appellees did not deny that the appellants had issued promissory notes, but the substantive content of these notes was equity transfer consideration, investment compensation, and entrusted payment of project costs. 3. The appellants' claim that the equity transfer between them and the appellees constituted a transfer for security had no factual or legal basis. The only statutory form of providing security with company equity is a pledge of equity. A pledge of equity and an equity transfer are two completely different types of civil legal acts. An equity transfer results in a change of shareholders or shares, whereas a pledge of equity does not cause such a change; the two are incompatible. 4. The appellants' allegation on appeal that Hongrong Company was still "controlled, managed, invested, and operated" by them was completely inconsistent with objective facts. After the equity transfer was completed, the "Chuangxiang Tiandi" project developed by Hongrong Company was fully taken over by the appellees, who have continued to invest and develop it to date. 5. The appellants' investment in the "Chuangxiang Tiandi" project before the equity transfer had been fully compensated, and all construction outcomes of that project were attributable to the appellees' contributions.

Upon hearing the appeal, the High People's Court of Jiangxi Province confirmed the facts found by the court of first instance.

Further facts were found: The funds involved in this dispute totaled RMB 73,294,000, for which promissory notes were issued. The 33 promissory notes were each explicitly stated to be used for purposes such as project costs, repayment of loans, payment of deposits, daily expenses of Hongrong Company, surveying fees, regulatory fees, advertising fees, decoration fees, etc.

After the change of equity registration in Hongrong Company, the appellant Xiong Zhimin continued to be responsible for the company's daily operation and management until August 2015.

Between December 22, 2014, and April 14, 2019, the parties engaged in numerous communications regarding the disputed funds, the equity transfer, the operation of Hongrong Company, and the resolution of the dispute. The appellant Xiong Zhimin provided 22 audio recordings, and the appellees Xu Ying and Li Changyou confirmed the authenticity of these recordings.

Further facts disclosed on appeal: The appellee Xu Ying and Li Changyou were in a cohabitation relationship. The appellee Yu Xiaoping was the brother-in-law of Li Changyou's former wife.

The issues in dispute were: 1. How should the nature of the "Equity Transfer Agreements" in question be characterized? 2. Should the claims of the appellants Xiong Zhimin and Ouke Company for confirmation of their equity and for the change of industrial and commercial registration be upheld?

The High People's Court of Jiangxi Province held on appeal:

I. On the Nature of the "Equity Transfer Agreements" in Question

An equity transfer for security is a form of security where the debtor or a third party (the transferor for security) transfers the company's equity to the creditor or a third party (the holder of the equity for security) to secure the debtor's obligation. Upon repayment of the debt, the equity is to be transferred back to the transferor for security. If the debt is not properly performed, the holder of the equity for security may obtain priority satisfaction from the equity. Formally, an equity transfer for security and an equity transfer both have the appearance of a change in equity and share certain similarities. However, the purpose of an equity transfer for security is to provide security for a debt, not to transfer the equity. The equity acquired by the holder of the equity for security is not a complete right; its actual content must not exceed the purpose of providing security. The holder is only a nominal shareholder. Although in this case, the appellees Xu Ying and Yu Xiaoping accepted the equity and completed the industrial and commercial registration change, giving them the appearance of holding equity, when considered in light of the creditor-debtor relationship and the true intent of the parties, the "Equity Transfer Agreements" in question should be characterized as an equity transfer for security.

First, a creditor-debtor relationship existed between the parties to the equity transfer. The funds involved in this dispute totaled RMB 73,294,000, for which promissory notes were issued. The appellees argued that promissory notes do not necessarily indicate a loan relationship, claiming that the actual content was equity transfer consideration, prior investment compensation, and entrusted payment of project costs. However, the documents, in their outward appearance, were all promissory notes, and each was marked with purposes related to project construction. None were marked as equity transfer consideration, prior investment compensation, remuneration, or project investment. In the audio recordings of communications between the appellants and appellees, these matters were never mentioned; instead, issues of borrowing and repayment were repeatedly discussed. The appellees also failed to provide other evidence proving that the funds in question were used for such purposes. Moreover, the appellees could not demonstrate how the equity transfer consideration and prior investment compensation were determined. The claimed method of paying "re-employment remuneration" to Xiong Zhimin was contradictory. It was also inconsistent with common sense that all operational payments of the company after the equity purchase were made through loans from Xiong Zhimin to the appellees. Therefore, the funds in question should be recognized as loans based on the promissory notes.

Second, the parties to the equity transfer had the intention to create a security arrangement, not a genuine transfer of equity.

1. In terms of communications between the parties: (a) The transferor repeatedly indicated that the equity was for security purposes and did not express an intention to transfer the equity; the transferee also repeatedly stated that it did not want the equity. (b) The equity in question was subject to a condition of return, i.e., the equity would be returned upon repayment of the loan principal and interest. (c) After the dispute arose, the parties continued to discuss equity cooperation and a buyout of the equity, indicating that the equity of Hongrong Company had not actually been fully acquired. Ultimately, the parties failed to reach an agreement, and accordingly, the equity of Hongrong Company was not actually transferred.

2. In terms of the actual performance of the "Equity Transfer Agreements": (a) The account books and project permits of Hongrong Company's operations were not actually transferred to the appellees, nor did the appellees provide evidence that such a transfer was agreed upon. (b) The appellees admitted that after the company was handed over, Xiong Zhimin was responsible for its operation and management until August 2015. Although the appellees claimed that Xiong Zhimin was "re-employed" by them, they did not enter into a re-employment contract with Xiong Zhimin. During the appellate hearing, they admitted that they never issued any operational instructions to Xiong Zhimin. They also lacked evidence to prove the payment of the claimed remuneration to Xiong Zhimin and failed to provide evidence such as social insurance records that could establish an employment relationship. Therefore, their claim of re-employing Xiong Zhimin could not be sustained. Considering the above, even after the "Equity Transfer Agreements" were signed and the registration change was completed, until August 2015, the transferee did not actually take over the management and operation of the company, which was inconsistent with a genuine equity transfer.

In light of the above analysis, the true intent of the "Equity Transfer Agreements" in this case was not to transfer the equity but to provide security for the debt. Therefore, they should be characterized as an equity transfer for security.

II. On Whether the Claims of the Appellants Xiong Zhimin and Ouke Company for Confirmation of Their Equity and for the Change of Industrial and Commercial Registration Should Be Upheld

Regarding the issue of confirming the equity of the appellants Xiong Zhimin and Ouke Company:

First, the true beneficial owner should be protected. Based on the analysis above, the true intent of Xiong Zhimin and Ouke Company in entering into the "Equity Transfer Agreements" and registering the equity in the names of Xu Ying and Yu Xiaoping was to effect an equity transfer for security, not a genuine equity transfer. Although the shareholders registered with the industrial and commercial authority are Xu Ying and Yu Xiaoping, such registration is a public notice and has evidentiary effect. Whether the equity has been transferred should be determined based on the true intent and facts. Therefore, Xu Ying and Yu Xiaoping are only nominal shareholders, not actual shareholders. Their rights should not exceed the purpose of providing security through the equity. Xiong Zhimin and Ouke Company have not lost their shareholder rights, and their true rights should be confirmed. Furthermore, based on the actual circumstances of this case, after August 2015, Xiong Zhimin and Ouke Company could not manage the company's operations. This situation has resulted in the nominal shareholder depriving the actual shareholder of the freedom to manage the company through the security mechanism, also affecting the actual shareholder's ability to use the sales proceeds from the "Chuangxiang Tiandi" project developed by Hongrong Company to repay the loans. Therefore, Xiong Zhimin and Ouke Company should be confirmed as the true shareholders of Hongrong Company.

Second, confirming Xiong Zhimin and Ouke Company as the true shareholders does not prejudice the appellees' security rights. In this case, the equity has already been registered in the appellees' names. The appellants and appellees had also reached an agreement during their communications that the appellees would hold the company seal and bank account of Hongrong Company. The appellees have sufficient means to protect their security rights. Confirming Xiong Zhimin and Ouke Company as the true shareholders does not affect the protection they receive under the transfer-for-security arrangement.

Finally, the appellees' investments after August 2015 do not affect the appellants' rights. The appellees claimed that starting from August 2015, they made substantial investments in the "Chuangxiang Tiandi" project in their capacity as shareholders and therefore should hold the equity. However, an equity transfer must be based on mutual agreement between the parties. The appellees' unilateral intent in making subsequent construction investments is irrelevant to whether they hold shareholder rights. The appellees are not the true shareholders of Hongrong Company, and their investments were not authorized or confirmed by the true shareholders. Their capital contributions will need to be settled and reconciled with the appellants, and they may assert such claims separately. In conclusion, it should be confirmed that Xiong Zhimin holds 49% of the equity of Hongrong Company and Ouke Company holds 51% of the equity of Hongrong Company.

Regarding the issue of handling the change of industrial and commercial registration. The equity transfer for guarantee is established based on the mutual agreement of the parties, and the content of their rights and obligations is determined in accordance with the parties' intentions. Although Yu Xiaoping and Xu Ying are only nominal shareholders, the Appellant and the Appellee entered into the "Equity Transfer Agreement" and registered the equity in the names of Yu Xiaoping and Xu Ying, thereby creating a transfer for guarantee. This reflects the true intentions of both parties, does not violate mandatory legal provisions, and such agreement is binding on both parties. At the same time, based on the communications between the parties, it has been agreed that the equity may be registered back in the Appellant's name only after the debts involved in the case are fully repaid. The Appellant has not yet fully repaid the debts involved, so the condition for transferring the equity back to the Appellant's name has not been fulfilled. If the equity were transferred back to the Appellant's name at this time, it would deprive the Appellee's claims of the protection afforded by the equity transfer for guarantee. Therefore, the Appellant's request for handling the change of industrial and commercial registration is not supported.

In summary, the Appellant's appeal is partially sustained and should be supported. The first-instance judgment had unclear findings of fact and erroneous application of law, which should be corrected. Pursuant to Article 60, paragraph 1 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 65, paragraph 1 and Article 170, paragraph 1, item 2 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the Jiangxi High People's Court rendered the following judgment on May 28, 2020:

1. Set aside the civil judgment (2019) Gan 02 Min Chu No. 85 of the Jingdezhen Intermediate People's Court, Jiangxi Province;

2. Confirm that Xiong Zhimin holds 49% of the equity of Jingdezhen Hongrong Real Estate Development Co., Ltd., and Kunming O'Ke Commerce and Trade Co., Ltd. holds 51% of the equity of Jingdezhen Hongrong Real Estate Development Co., Ltd.;

3. Dismiss the other claims of Xiong Zhimin and Kunming O'Ke Commerce and Trade Co., Ltd.

This judgment is final.
